ghi: THAM KHẢO — không phải chấm đạt; chủ dự án chấm cuối (§13.4)

tra_loi.Q1: A huge fire. The caption reads '1666 — The Great Fire', and flames and smoke spread over the dense timber city from 2 Sept 1666.
tra_loi.Q2: It starts in one small place. A baker's oven glows in a bakery, labelled 'Thomas Farriner, baker to the King'. A map then highlights a small patch near Pudding Lane and London Bridge. From there the fire spreads across the whole riverside city over several days.
tra_loi.Q3: They flee and carry their goods away. People load bundles and chests onto carts and push through crowded streets. Crowds pile belongings into rowing boats on the river. Some cross the bridge on foot. Afterwards, refugees camp in open fields with tents.
tra_loi.Q4: Not sure. The big church on the hill is never clearly shown burning. Around 4 Sept a large building stands amid the flames (frames 49-50), and a church tower is among the ruins afterwards (frame 69). That is all I can see.
tra_loi.Q5: Brick houses with red roofs, built with scaffolding and bricklayers. They go up on the old street layout. A planner (Christopher Wren) shows a grand new street plan, but the later 3D views show the old lanes kept. A court-like scene suggests the plans were argued over.
tra_loi.Q6: A big white domed cathedral rises above the red roofs, built from about 1708 to 1711. A tall stone column (the Monument, '202 ft') stands near the river. The dome is labelled '365 ft' and the caption reads 'The dome rules the skyline'.
tra_loi.Q7: On the night of 29 Dec 1940 the city is bombed and burns again; the caption is 'The second great fire'. Firefighters battle the flames, and about 100,000 incendiaries are counted. The domed cathedral still stands glowing amid the fire. A damaged area is outlined afterwards, then rebuilt with the same streets.
tra_loi.Q8: A modern city of glass towers and office blocks beside the river, shown by day and lit up at night. The old domed cathedral is still visible among the towers. A few older red-brick buildings remain.

lac.why: A large building in the flames is unclear. It is not obvious whether it is the hilltop church or what happens to it.
Wren's plan and the new layout are hard to follow without words, and the rebuilt streets look like the old ones.
The film suddenly jumps back to 1676 and 1647 with no explanation.
A sudden jump back to 1666 after 1938 is confusing.

tra_loi.Q1: A huge city fire. The on-screen text says "1666 — The Great Fire", and the fire spreads for days, from 2 to 7 Sept 1666.
tra_loi.Q2: One small place. It starts in a bakery with an oven fire, labelled "Thomas Farriner, baker to the King". A map highlights a small spot near Pudding Lane and London Bridge. From there it spreads through the packed wooden houses along the river.
tra_loi.Q3: They flee on foot with bundles, carts and wagons piled with belongings. They load their goods into rowing boats and cross the river. They watch the blaze from the water and the far bank. Some camp in open fields with tents and campfires. A bridge also appears crowded with people. Fire-fighting is not clearly shown.
tra_loi.Q4: Not sure. Around frames 49-50 (196-200 s) a large church-like building with a tower sits in the middle of the blaze, and it looks engulfed in flames. The pictures do not clearly show it burning down or being destroyed. A church tower stands amid the ruins in the frames after the fire (frame 69). Whether it is the church on the hill is not certain.
tra_loi.Q5: In brick. A big orange outline shows the burnt area, and the ruins are surveyed. Christopher Wren is shown with a plan, and builders work with bricks and scaffolding. The city is rebuilt with red-brick houses. The new street layout is mostly the old street pattern, not Wren's grand plan: the 1666 plan appears as a small engraved inset, and the 1946 caption reads "same streets" for the second rebuild. One wide new street appears around 1673-77.
tra_loi.Q6: A large white-stone cathedral with a dome appears, shown as a tall building of 365 ft. It is finished around 1710-11 under the caption "The dome rules the skyline". A tall free-standing column appears next to the brick houses (1673-75), labelled 202 ft and shown in an engraving as "The Monument".
tra_loi.Q7: Bombing at night in 1940, captioned "the second great fire" (29-30 Dec 1940). Firefighters hose fires from a muddy riverbank and on rooftops. The city is shown burning, with a counter of 100,000 incendiaries. A large area is outlined in orange. The domed cathedral still stands among the flames and survives. Much of the surrounding city is damaged.
tra_loi.Q8: A modern city of glass and concrete towers and office blocks beside the river, with bridges. The domed cathedral is still visible among the towers. At night the towers' windows glow. A final text card says the film was made from the 1666 survey and old engravings.

lac.why: Nearly black frames with no visible action, so I could not tell what was happening.
The date jumps back to 1647 and an engraving appears, with no obvious reason in the pictures.
An engulfed building in the flames, with no sign saying which church it is or what happens to it.
Dark map-like views of the street layout with no explanation.
Judges at a table with documents, and the point is unclear.
The date jumps back (1676, 1647) with no explanation.
The date jumps back to 1666 just before 1940, then returns to 1940.
The date jumps back to 7 Sept 1666 in the middle of the 1941 scenes.
The date suddenly shows 2 Sept 1666 again after 2026, with the fire returning at the end.

tra_loi.Q1: A great city fire. A caption reads 'The Great Fire' (1666). Flames spread through the dense wooden, half-timbered houses over several days, from 2 to 5 Sept 1666.
tra_loi.Q2: One small place. It starts in a single bakery with an oven fire (a baker is named on screen). It then shows a narrow street with a few houses burning, and only afterwards the fire spreading across the wider district. A map near the river marks the small start area (a lane near the bridge).
tra_loi.Q3: They flee on foot and in carts piled with bundles and furniture. They load belongings into rowing boats and escape across the Thames. Crowds also cross the bridge. Survivors end up camping in open fields in tents beside small fires. The pictures show no organised firefighting in 1666.
tra_loi.Q4: Not sure. Around frames 49–50 (196–200s) a large church-like building with a tower stands in the glowing, burning city. The pictures do not clearly show it burning or collapsing. Later a ruined church tower stands among the rubble (frame 69).
tra_loi.Q5: In brick, with scaffolding and brick-laying shown, and some stone. It is rebuilt largely on the old street layout. A surveyor with stakes marks out plots, and a court-like hearing is held, apparently about plots or boundaries. A plan with a new regular grid is shown, but the finished city has an irregular layout like the old one.
tra_loi.Q6: A large white domed cathedral rises over the red-brick roofs, with its dome completed around 1710–11. A caption reads 'The dome rules the skyline'. A tall stone column (the Monument, labelled 202 ft) stands near the river and is shown with an engraving.
tra_loi.Q7: Bombing sets the city on fire again. Dated 29–30 Dec 1940 and captioned 'The second great fire', the night sky glows with fire, firefighters work at the river and on rooftops, and a count of incendiaries appears. The big domed cathedral still stands lit amid the flames. A large area is burnt and marked in orange.
tra_loi.Q8: A modern city, 2026, of glass and concrete towers and office blocks beside the river with bridges. By night the windows are lit. The old domed cathedral is still visible among the towers.
